items.title: George Blanchin Interview, 1959-11-13
items.q: No, I would say more of the school of Pierron or possibly the old tuxedo bands of Celestan and Wrigley.

ctx.x: Well, in those days, I'll tell you, one of the most sought-after bands in that part of the country was the Claven Williams Band, from Donisonville. I wish I could tell you more about it, but I can't, other than that it was very much in demand. And as I recall it, they had a rather large band. I think they used eight or ten pieces.
Would they be of the school of Pierron or more like Buddy Petit?
No, I would say more of the school of Pierron or possibly the old tuxedo bands of Celestan and Wrigley.
